paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: the way back to the LORD is already open, and He is the One who holds the door. Look at how this chapter starts. "Return, O Israel, to the LORD your God, for you have stumbled by your iniquity." (Hosea 14:1) He doesn't leave Israel guessing, either. He hands them the words to say, and then He answers, "I will heal their apostasy; I will freely love them, for My anger has turned away from them." (Hosea 14:4)

Now hear what that means for you, baker. Israel is told to say, "Assyria will not save us, nor will we ride on horses." (Hosea 14:3) Everything we lean on besides the LORD is a wobbly stool, and coming home means letting go of the stool. And what do we get? A God who says, "It is I who answer and watch over him." (Hosea 14:8) That's a whole lot better than a stool, friend, and it's the kind of love you don't have to earn first.

Then comes the part I'd pin on the fridge. The LORD says, "your fruit comes from Me." (Hosea 14:8) Blossoms, roots, shade, fragrance, all of it grows because He is the dew, not because we squeezed it out ourselves. The last verse says the ways of the LORD are right, "and the righteous walk in them but the rebellious stumble in them." (Hosea 14:9) So when you stumble, and you will, I sure did, you know where to go: back to Him, with your confessions in hand, and let Him do the growing.
